description: Tame in a way nothing wild is: it comes closer than it should, bolts, and bites in earnest when it cannot run.
lore: White is a poor colour in country that has things hunting in it, and the coat is not the strange part. The strange part is that it comes toward you. Nothing wild does that. A rabbit has decided in advance about every noise there is, and this one decides right about all of them, and then for a moment decides wrong: three or four steps in your direction, ears up, the way an animal moves toward a person it is expecting — then whatever is left inside catches up with it, and it is forty feet away. Somebody kept this one. The somebody got forgotten before the rabbit did.

Twice a day it comes out onto the same patch of open ground within sight of [[lore/the_waking|the meadow]], faces the same way, and waits. Nothing arrives. [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] can see the spot from the fire, and when the fire can spare her she goes and sits at it — a little way off, at the hour, saying nothing. It will not take food from her; she is the wrong person, and it knows that better than it knows anything. She goes anyway. She has met strangers at their worst hour her whole watch, and she says a kept hour should not have to be kept alone.

It will not turn while it still has somewhere to run. Take that away and it turns, and the teeth were always real. Most first seasons include this lesson, the gentlest on offer: nearly everything in this country will hurt you eventually, and almost none of it means to.
gm_notes: Solveig's line is her whole biography in small — she keeps a meeting nobody comes to, same as the rabbit. Play the hour scene quiet; the rabbit never takes the food, and she never stops bringing it.
